folkways.perk.building_fortune.desc: Blocks broken with a tool drop as if it had Fortune I/II/III; a tool with higher Fortune keeps its own. Prospecting finds are unaffected.
folkways.perk.building_prospecting.desc: Mining ordinary stone has an 4/7/11%% chance to find a mineral weighted by the local biome, height and ore generation settings. Rank III has a 15%% chance of a second find.
folkways.perk.building_quarrying.desc: Consecutive mining of the same ordinary stone builds up to +15/30/50%% excavation speed after 8 blocks. A 10-second pause resets momentum.
folkways.perk.building_tool_expert.desc: Building and excavation tool durability consumption -15/30/45%%.
folkways.perk.crafting_batch.desc: Complete 2/3/4 runs of one recipe per operation, consuming all materials.
folkways.perk.crafting_byproducts.desc: Eligible recipes have a 10%%/20%%/30%% chance to yield their configured byproduct.
folkways.perk.crafting_frugal.desc: Eligible recipes refund each ingredient unit with an 5%%/10%%/15%% chance; packing recipes excluded.
folkways.perk.crafting_furnace.desc: Input batches personally loaded smelt 10%%/20%%/30%% faster.
folkways.perk.farming_bountiful.desc: Primary crop yield +10%% / 20%% / 35%%. Separate seed drops are unchanged.
folkways.perk.farming_care.desc: Planted and replanted crops grow 10%% / 20%% / 35%% faster. One treatment per crop.
folkways.perk.farming_chain_harvest.desc: Harvest 1 / 2 / 4 additional adjacent mature crops in the field, respecting reserved jobs.
folkways.perk.farming_replant.desc: Replant during harvest, saving 0%% / 15%% / 30%% of seeds.
folkways.perk.fishing_school.desc: Fish catches have a 15%% / 25%% / 40%% chance of 1 / 1 / 2 extra fish of the same species.
folkways.perk.fishing_treasure.desc: Successful catches have a 2%% / 4%% / 6%% chance of an extra local discovery, controlled by loot tables.
folkways.perk.fishing_water_sense.desc: Progressively favors uncommon fish from the active local fishing loot table.
folkways.perk.herding_breeder.desc: Resident-assisted breeding has a 5%% / 10%% / 20%% chance of twins, within the pasture target.
folkways.perk.herding_butcher.desc: Ordinary carcass products +15%% / 30%% / 50%%. Special drops are unchanged.
folkways.perk.herding_fleece.desc: Shearing yields 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 extra wool of the original color on average.
folkways.perk.herding_nurture.desc: Feeding a juvenile additionally reduces remaining growth time by 10%% / 20%% / 30%%, once per animal.
folkways.perk.patrolling_alert.desc: Detect threats 2/4/6 blocks farther away and share targets with nearby patrollers.
folkways.perk.patrolling_martial.desc: Deal 10%%/20%%/35%% more damage to hostile creatures.
folkways.perk.patrolling_reassuring.desc: Wards grant residents +2/4/6 safety mood and make attack distress fade 20%%/40%%/60%% faster.
folkways.perk.patrolling_stalwart.desc: Take 5%%/10%%/20%% less damage from hostile creatures.

folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.header: Building: draw it, and the colony builds it
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_1: Mark out a box or draw a line with the book, then right-click and choose Pattern.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_2: Choose a pattern and its settings, down to the blocks it uses. Add your own patterns in the folkways/pattern folder or a data pack.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_3: Builders take the order. First they clear whatever is in the way, from the top down. Containers are emptied into storage first.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_4: Then they build from the bottom up, with blocks from the colony's storage.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_5: Hold the book to see the missing blocks as ghosts. A card above the site shows progress and what it Still needs.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_6: Where a block is out of reach, they put up scaffolding from storage and take it down afterwards.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_7: Build orders are listed under Facilities. Cancel on an order's card stops the work and removes its scaffolding.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_8: A mine is planned all at once from the ground as it stands, as one ordinary build order.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_9: In creative mode, Build now places it instantly.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.creative_supplie: Creative supplies: only what the task needs
In creative mode, place a creative supply box and set it to offer all items, or an allowlist of items, tags and searches.
Take in the box with the book to supply tasks. Take in a plain chest too, for finished goods.
Residents take only what their current job needs. If their pack is full or the box is out of reach, they wait.
To test a full production chain, allowlist only raw ingredients and order the final dish. Residents must make everything in between.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.damage_control.t: Mark two corners with the book, right-click and choose Damage control to protect the area. Residents need the Damage control trade; fleeing danger still comes first.
Workers smother nearby fires by hand. With Create: FireFighting Additions, they prefer a hydrant cabinet with a hose, nozzle and water, or borrow and refill an extinguisher.
Right-click the area to open its card. Click Reset baseline, then turn on repairs. Hover the colored markers to see fires, missing blocks, conflicts and workers.
Containers, crops, fluids and machines are not recorded. Changed blocks show as conflicts. After rebuilding, click Reset baseline again.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dining.header: Dining: set a table for the colony
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dining.text_1: Mark out the tables and the chairs beside them, then right-click and choose Dining area. Use tables from a supported mod; bottom stairs work as chairs. Leave an aisle beside the chairs.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dining.text_2: Table tops joined on one level form one table. Residents serve from any reachable edge and eat at any free chair.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dining.text_3: On the card, choose Table food and Servings per tabletop block (1–4). Tables without storage hold one placed food, such as a cake.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dining.text_4: Residents bring the food from storage, or have it made, and set the table. Hungry residents take a free seat and eat.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dining.text_5: Bar drinks is a separate list. Supported bar counters in the area restock themselves, and diners fetch a drink with their meal. Plain bar cabinets need delivery orders.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.header: Farming: mark a plot, and it keeps going
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_1: Click two opposite corners, then right-click and choose Farm. On its card, choose the Crop, wheat here. Clear grass and Clear flowers start on.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_2: Residents hoe the ground inside. Farm must allow a hoe under Settings → Trade tools.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_3: Then they sow, and come back when the crop is ripe. Crops that need no farmland, like cane or saplings, are planted without hoeing.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_4: Most crops leave bare soil when harvested, and the next round is sown in place.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_5: Sugar cane is cut at three tall and bamboo at four, leaving the bottom stalk to regrow. Bamboo goes in two rows with an aisle between.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_6: For melons and pumpkins, only the fruit is taken and the stem grows more. Stems go one block in from the edge, leaving room for fruit.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_7: A farm of saplings is a wood lot. Whole trees are felled with their leaves, and saplings are replanted. Dark oak, jungle and spruce can go in 2×2.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_8: A farmer with the Replant perk resows with seeds from the harvest. This only works for crops cut whole, like wheat.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.header: Fishing: mark the bank, not the water
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.text_1: A fishery marks out the bank where residents stand.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.text_2: Not the water. They fish the water they can reach from the bank.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.text_3: Each fishery fishes the nearest water block, and two never share one. If it is taken, the second fishery stays idle.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.text_4: Fishers need a fishing rod allowed under Settings → Trade tools.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.text_5: Then they wait for a bite. The line to the bobber shows they are fishing, not idling.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.text_6: The Skilled Angler perk makes fish bite sooner.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.groundwork.heade: Groundwork: clear, fill and tidy an area
folkways_vanilla.ponder.groundwork.text_: With Clear or Fill ticked, the area becomes one build order and then disappears. Other ticked jobs are ignored.
Clear alone empties every block in the area. Builders dig it out like any building site.
Fill replaces every block in the area with the block you chose. Builders bring it from storage.
With Clear and Fill off, Weed has farmers pull grass and ferns. Flowers go only if Pull flowers is ticked.
Fell trees cuts down trees whose trunks stand inside, leaves and all, plus fallen logs on the ground. Colony buildings are left alone.
Haul has haulers pick up loose items in the area and take them to storage.
Forage has farmers harvest food plants and keep every drop. Young berry bushes and cave vines are cleared too and do not regrow. If Clear is also ticked, Clear wins.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_1: Take in beds with the book. Residents claim free beds on their own.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_2: Walking and work tire residents out. When tired, they go to their own bed to sleep. Without a bed they cannot sleep, and their mood drops.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_3: Work and walking use up food. Time spent working and distance walked add up to fatigue.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_4: Each resident carries three days of food and eats when hungry. Choose allowed food under Settings → Food and daily needs.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_5: With no allowed food in storage, packs stay empty, and a starving resident loses health.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_6: Hold the book to see a card over each resident: a drumstick for fullness and a moon for rest.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_7: Hold the book to see a card over each bed: who sleeps there, the room grade and how to improve it.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.header: Housing: a room worth coming home to
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.text_1: Put beds in an enclosed room with a roof and a door residents can walk through. Every floor block needs light level 8. Otherwise, or with under 4 floor blocks per bed, it is a Basic bed.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.text_2: A Suitable dormitory has 4 floor blocks per bed. Comfortable housing needs 6 per bed, at most 4 beds and 2 kinds of furnishing.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.text_3: An Excellent bedroom needs 9 per bed, at most 2 beds and 3 kinds of furnishing, one of them decoration. The kinds are storage, carpets, decoration, tables and lighting; copies of one kind count once.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.text_4: Keep work blocks such as crafting tables and furnaces out of an Excellent bedroom. Hold the book to read each bed's grade and advice.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.text_5: The icon after a resident's name shows mood: sad below 40, neutral from 40, happy from 70. With the book held, sparks show when something raises or lowers it.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.text_6: Mood sets work speed: ×0.75 at 0, normal at 60, ×1.15 at 100. Food, rest, housing, company and recreation all help.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.header: Orders: say what to keep in stock
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_1: An order keeps one item stocked in one container. Right-click one of the colony's chests with the book to open its card.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_2: Under Replenishment order, set the Item, a Min and a Target.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_3: Maintain keeps it stocked: below Min, it refills to Target. Once fills to Target a single time, then the order is done.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_4: Order the finished goods. The colony fetches the materials and works them at its crafting table, stonecutter or smithing table.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_5: Smelting uses the colony's furnaces, blast furnaces and smokers, fed from the Fuel list in Settings: coal and charcoal by default.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_6: No one goes mining for an order. If storage has neither the goods nor their materials, it waits.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_7: To remove an order, open the chest's card and click Del next to it under Orders here.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_8: Item filter and Accept storage only limit what residents store there day to day. Orders always deliver.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.header: Pastures: keep a herd, harvest the rest
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_1: Mark out a pasture like a farm. On its card, choose the Animal (cows, sheep, pigs or chickens), Retained adults (0–64) and Shear wool.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_2: Young animals count toward the herd, but only grown ones count as retained adults.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_3: At or below the target, residents feed adults in pairs to breed them. At the target, one extra young is allowed; feeding then waits until it grows up.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_4: Only grown animals above the target are culled: keep four with six grown cows, and two are culled. A target of 0 culls every grown animal.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_5: Cows are milked only when the colony needs milk, once per cow per day.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_6: With Shear wool on, sheep are shorn when their wool grows back; shears must be allowed under Settings → Trade tools. Eggs are picked up where they land.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_7: A gap in the fence shows in red on the pasture's card. Animals that wander out stop counting, and the pasture breeds back up.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.recreation.text_: In free time, residents stroll nearby. Among flowers they stop to relax, which restores more recreation than walking.
Chatting with neighbors and playing with pets help too. Residents choose these themselves, and may take a short break when recreation runs very low.
Pets may visit once three residents have beds in a Suitable dormitory or better. Each half day brings a chance, with mob spawning on and a safe spot nearby.
One pet per three well-housed residents: cats from three, wolves from six, parrots from ten. They arrive untamed. Residents also play with pets tamed by colony members.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.header: Residents: who comes, what they do, how they look
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_1: In Survival, a newcomer needs a registered free bed and stored food for everyone plus one.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_2: Someone must also be waiting. Newcomers gather over time, more slowly as the colony grows. Click Let one in on Workforce to admit the next.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_3: On Workforce, each resident has a cell per trade. Click to allow or forbid it; scroll to set its priority, 1 to 4. You rank trades, not tasks.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_4: Working earns experience. Each level draws a perk for that trade; levels 3, 6 and 10 also draw a shared perk. The resident's window lists trades, levels and perks.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_5: Newcomers get a name and look from the colony's Name pool and Look pool, which you edit from Workforce. A resident's own window can change both.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_6: Hit by a mob or player, or set on fire, a resident drops what they are doing and runs.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_7: When a resident dies, every colony member is told.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_1: With Take in picked, left-click a crafting table, stonecutter or smithing table to add it as a station. Furnaces, blast furnaces and smokers work the same way.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_2: A station needs a spot within reach and in view where a resident can stand. A fully walled-in station is skipped.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_3: Residents with the Craft trade work them, making what orders need with ingredients from storage.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_4: The stonecutter uses its own recipes. The smithing table is only used for upgrades, never trims.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_5: At a furnace, they load a batch and come back when it is done. Big batches are split across idle furnaces of the same kind.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_6: A loaded furnace that goes out gets one piece of fuel at a time, only from the Fuel list: coal and charcoal by default.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_7: Finished items nobody is waiting for are taken out too, to make room.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_8: Facilities lists every station; click one to open its card. The Fuel list is in Settings.

folkways.mechanics.zone.folkways_vanilla: Grow, tend and harvest the selected crops.
Clear, fell, gather, fill and level ground as configured.
Breed, shear, milk and cull while retaining the chosen adult count.
Walk the ordered route, deter monster spawning and fight nearby threats.
Stock tables and serve residents seated at reachable chairs.
Collect honey bottles or honeycomb from full hives with campfire smoke.
Restore grass and collect planting materials as configured.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_chain.he: One order, every step: wheat to noodles
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_chain.te: Order only the final dish, such as udon, and take in every station along the way. The colony plans the flour, dough and noodles itself.
The millstone grinds wheat into flour. Leave room to walk around it and a clear way out.
At the crafting table, flour and a water bucket make dough. The empty bucket goes back to storage.
A borrowed kitchen knife cuts the dough into three noodles on the chopping board. Then the knife goes back.
The stockpot also needs its soup base, the other ingredients, a lid and a bowl.
The order is done when the finished dish reaches storage. A missing ingredient or tool makes that step wait.
Spare noodles stay for later orders. Drying, steaming and tea chains work the same way: give them stations, clear paths and raw ingredients.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_equipmen: Gathering grass seeds borrows a straw hat, wears it and returns it after. A hat in a pack does nothing, and other work never asks for one.
Farming clothes have their own allowed list. Water-farming tasks may borrow a full set and return it after. Clothes a resident already wears are never swapped.
Farms pick by hand by default: tea regrows from age 3, tomato and chili from age 5. Set the farm's Harvest method to Sickle to cut whole plants.
The sickle is borrowed for the task and cuts only the claimed crop, never a neighbor's field.
Knives, kitchen shovels and sickles are shared colony tools. If there is none, one is made; if it is in use, other work waits. Afterwards it goes back to a rack or storage.
Cookery's water movement bonus needs all four farmer pieces worn. Water tasks borrow the whole set; a hat alone only adds seed drops.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_heat.hea: Kitchen heat: light, shelter and relight
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_heat.tex: Take in the stove as a kitchen station. The colony keeps it lit; the pot on top does the cooking.
Lighting uses one flint and steel use or one fire charge. A lit stove needs no more fuel.
Any lit heat source works, and so do heat blocks such as magma.
Rain or water can put the stove out. Residents wait until it is dry instead of wasting fire starters.
Keep the stove's front and a standing spot clear. Once it is dry under shelter, residents relight it.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_millston: The millstone: turn it, then walk clear
The whole millstone is one kitchen station. A flour order brings wheat and sends a resident to grind it.
Leave room to walk around the mill and a clear way out. Residents check the exit before loading.
Passers-by are not caught. Only the assigned resident is hitched to turn the mill.
When grinding ends, the resident is let go, and the task waits until they walk clear.
Only then is the flour collected into storage.
Cancelling or reloading frees the resident safely and keeps the ingredients. A blocked exit waits for a path. Animal-driven mills work as usual.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_orders.h: A colony kitchen: order the final dish
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_orders.t: Take in the kitchen stations, a crafting table and storage. Leave a reachable standing spot beside each station.
Give residents the Craft trade, then order the finished dish. The colony works out the ingredients and steps.
Keep raw ingredients, containers and kitchen tools in reachable storage. If something is missing, the task waits without using anything up.
Each kitchen station's card shows what it is doing. The other lessons here cover heat, tools, milling, cooking and farming.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_pots.hea: Pots and stockpots: ingredients, heat and bowls
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_pots.tex: Take in each pot as a kitchen station and keep its heat lit. Leave the stir-fry pot's handle side clear; residents stand there. Food you put in yourself is left alone.
A stir-fry first checks it has all the food, one oil and any bowls. Then the resident adds the oil and ingredients.
The resident borrows a kitchen shovel and stirs as the recipe asks. Dishes that need bowls wait for all of them; others come out with the shovel.
Collect stir-fry within 40 seconds or it burns; 20 seconds later it turns to charcoal. Burnt ingredients are not refunded.
A stockpot checks the soup base, food, lid and bowls first. The resident pours the base, adds the ingredients and closes the lid. It cooks only with heat and the lid on.
Open the lid and serve each portion into its bowl: three rice portions take three bowls. The next batch starts once the pot is empty.
Recipes match as they do in Cookery, and flexible dishes keep their quality. A cancelled or reloaded batch is recovered without spending ingredients again.

Normal orders use matching recipes. Only a Suspicious Stir-Fry or Dark Cuisine order uses unmatched ingredients, and only Dark Cuisine waits for burning. A normal dish that burns does not fill its order.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_rice.hea: Rice: from a flooded plot to a bowl
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_rice.tex: Mark out a farm on flooded dirt and supply a hoe. Residents till under the water, then sow. Keep water in the crop's block and two clear blocks above.
One wild rice seed plants a whole three-block rice plant. Residents prefer wild seeds but can plant edible rice instead.
A ripe plant is harvested once. The bottom part gives the panicles and seeds; the top two give nothing extra.
Harvesting leaves the water for replanting. Wild seeds and rice share one seed reserve, with wild seeds kept first.
Take in a reachable millstone. A rice order sends a resident to grind: one panicle gives three rice.
Order the finished rice meal. Residents link the paddy, millstone and heated stockpot. Supply bowls and a lid; without them the batch waits.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_seeds.he: Keep seeds, compost surplus, restore grass
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_seeds.te: Mark out an area, then right-click and choose Seed grassland. A farmer wearing a straw hat gathers its short grass only when grass seeds run low.
Drops use the normal chances. Plant your first rare seed to grow more. Other seeds need their own farms or recipes; grass cannot give every crop.
The Composting card in Settings turns automatic composting on or off and sets a seed reserve, 64 by default, or per seed. Seeds needed for sowing, on the way or ordered are never composted.
Take in a composter; no straw hat needed. Residents compost only a full batch of surplus: 21 wheat seeds fill an empty composter. Less than that waits.
The composter then ripens as usual. A resident collects the bone meal and empties it. With composting off, ripe bone meal is still collected.
With Restore short grass with bone meal on, residents use bone meal to regrow grass on a flat, safe 15×15 patch inside the area. Without bone meal or room, it waits.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_spit.hea: The shawarma spit: power, two halves, safe hands
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_spit.tex: Take in either half to add the whole spit as one kitchen station. Each half holds up to eight of the same ingredient.
Orders use an empty half and leave your own food alone.
A redstone signal turns the spit. Without power, cooking pauses.
When it is done, the booked resident takes the food safely with a kitchen knife. It does not make them fireproof or cut the power.
The cooked food goes to storage once. Cancelling or reloading recovers it without spending ingredients again.
The steamer: layers, lid and heat
A stack of steamers is one kitchen station. A half block holds four portions, a full block eight. Heat rises only through full blocks, up to four high.
A task takes one fully empty block and fills it in one go. Food in other blocks is left alone.
The resident closes the top lid. Lower layers are covered by the ones above; a half block under another steamer blocks the heat.
It still needs heat below. Without heat, the batch cools and waits.
Residents collect only when all their portions are steamed. Taking out empties the whole block, so a task never shares a block with you.
The food goes to storage once, and the lid is put back as it was. A changed batch is refused rather than breaking the steamer.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_teapot.h: Tea: a bucket, a tea bag and twelve cups
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_teapot.t: Take in a teapot and order the finished tea. Each brew makes twelve cups, so supply twelve empty cups and room to set them out.
The pot is filled with a bucket of the recipe's liquid: water for most teas, milk for milk tea. The empty bucket goes back.
Then the tea goes in. Brewing needs heat; without it, it pauses. Reloading never spends another bag or bucket.
Once brewed, the resident picks up the pot, sets out a cup, pours one and takes it. Cups you placed are left alone.
This repeats for all twelve. If serving fails, the pot is restored and only unused cups go back.
The empty pot goes back on its station. The twelve cups and the empty bucket go to storage once.
Normal orders use matching recipes. Only a Mystery Tea order uses unmatched ingredients. It brews longer and makes four cups, not twelve, so prepare four.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_tools.he: Shared kitchen tools: borrow and return
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_tools.te: Take in a kitchenware rack as storage. Its two slots each hold one tool; other storage is used when it is full.
Crafters don't each grab a knife. A task borrows the knife, shovel or sickle it needs and keeps it until done.
One knife, one user at a time. Other tasks wait for it; waiting never makes a second knife.
Returned tools go to an allowed rack first, then other storage, keeping their name, enchantments and wear.
A new tool is made only when no usable one exists and none is on its way. Tools are made before the food, so the first crafter can make the first knife.
To run two tasks at once, place a Maintain order for knives with Min and Target both at 2. Borrowed knives still count, so no extras are made.
Settings → Trade tools still decides which tools may be used. An empty list allows none, and more residents don't mean more tools.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_tray.hea: The bamboo tray: weather and timing
folkways_vanilla.ponder.cookery_tray.tex: Take in a bamboo tray and order something to dry or wet. A task uses one empty slot; your items in other slots stay put.
Drying needs open sky and dry weather. A solid roof pauses it; open air or clear glass lets it go on.
The tray runs on its own timer, and residents wait for it to finish.
Wetting needs rain or water dripping from a dripstone. Many changes reverse in other weather, so finished items are collected promptly.
Only the task's own result is taken; changed contents are refused. Dried leaves can then go into tea bags and brewing.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.tavern.header: Tavern: from the vineyard to a glass of wine
folkways_vanilla.ponder.tavern.text_1: Mark out a rectangular farm and choose grapevines. Supply trellises and vines. Residents raise a four-high post at each corner and a trellis roof five blocks up.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.tavern.text_2: Vines are planted at the posts, climb over the roof and hang grapes below. Residents pick the ripe ones. Leave room around the plot.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.tavern.text_3: Take in a pressing tub and a Tavern barrel as kitchen stations, allow the Craft trade and order wine. Eight grapes press into a bucket of juice. Supply buckets and empty bottles.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.tavern.text_4: The barrel takes four buckets from the top, so give residents a way up, such as a stepladder. Put a closed tap on its side with solid ground below. Once fermented, residents fill bottles one at a time.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.tavern.text_5: Bar cabinets taken in as storage are stocked by orders. Bar counters in a dining area restock from its Bar drinks; choose wine there.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.tavern.text_6: After a meal, a diner may fetch a bottle from the counter, or sit on a chair beside it for a drink. Drinking gives the wine's effects and leaves the empty bottle.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.carts.text_1: Draw a line through each station in turn, then right-click and choose Cart line. On its card, choose the Cart and the Route, Out and back or Loop. The colony makes the cart and sets it at the first station.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.carts.text_2: A hauler pulls the cart from station to station, stopping at each for loading. A supply cart takes a tame adult horse from a pasture, which then stops counting there. Leave wide gates and room at corners.

folkways.vocation.folkways_vanilla.condu: Takes the driver's seat of the colony's trains
folkways.vocation.folkways_vanilla.dispa: Sits at the stock keeper's desk so the colony can order from its parcel networks
folkways_vanilla.ponder.create_handoff.h: Handing a Create schematic to the colony
folkways_vanilla.ponder.create_handoff.t: With Create installed, a schematic placed with Create's tools can go to the colony instead of a schematicannon.
Hold the schematic, with the Colony Book in your other hand.
The schematic's tools now include Hand Off. Pick it and right-click.
A window asks what to do with cells the schematic leaves empty: Leave what stands there, or Dig out what stands there.
Click Place the build order. It goes where the schematic stands, rotated and mirrored as you set it.
From there it is a normal build order: residents build it, and it is listed under Facilities. It is never placed instantly, even in creative.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dispatch.header: Dispatch: order from a Create package network
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dispatch.text_1: Build a Create package network: stock behind a packager and a stock link, plus a Stock Ticker. Each packager must pass parcels to a frogport on one moving chain net, or to a postbox set to a station. Nothing else may take from those packagers.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dispatch.text_2: With Take in picked, left-click the stock link or Stock Ticker to take the network in. Left-click a frogport or chain conveyor to take in its chain net, or a postbox to take it in. Click again to give it back. Ordering starts once its shipping is taken in too.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dispatch.text_3: A network locked in Create can only be handed over by someone allowed to use it.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dispatch.text_4: The Stock Ticker is a desk. A resident with the Dispatch trade sits on a seat beside it, on the same level or one below.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dispatch.text_5: The colony orders only while its own keeper sits at the desk. Without one, stock is counted but cannot be ordered.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dispatch.text_6: Every frogport on a held chain net is a pick-up point, except those beside packagers and those over a container. So is every held postbox a colony train stops at. Addresses that are * or contain { } , \ are skipped.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dispatch.text_7: When the colony needs goods the network has, it orders them to the handiest pick-up point. A hauler waits there and unpacks the order.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dispatch.text_8: Parcels nobody here is waiting for are unpacked too, so they don't clog the pick-up point.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dispatch.text_9: Dispatch networks under Facilities show each network, whether someone is at the desk, its pick-up points and what is on the way.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.elevator.header: Elevators: walk in, ride and walk out
folkways_vanilla.ponder.elevator.text_1: Build and power a Create elevator: a glued cabin under an elevator pulley, a redstone contact on the cabin and elevator contacts at each floor. Leave walkable landings beside the shaft.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.elevator.text_2: With Take in picked, left-click the elevator pulley. Residents can then travel between its floors, wherever the cabin is.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.elevator.text_3: A resident waits on the landing and steps into a free spot when the cabin arrives. Capacity depends on clear floor space; seats add none.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.elevator.text_4: The cabin carries them to their floor, where they walk out and carry on. Keep the entrances clear.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.elevator.text_5: A full cabin leaves the next resident for a later trip. A stopped or overstressed drive carries no one.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.rail.header: Rail: give the colony a train to run
folkways_vanilla.ponder.rail.text_1: Build and assemble a train with Create as usual. The colony can run it for you.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.rail.text_2: With the Colony Book in your off hand, use a Train Schedule on the driver's seat of a train that has none. The colony takes the train on.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.rail.text_3: With the book still in your off hand, use an empty hand on the seat to take the schedule out and give the train back.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.rail.text_4: When the train stops at a station with an empty driver's seat, a resident with the Drive trade sits in it.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.rail.text_5: Give every stop a time delay long enough to board. Residents plan rides from the schedule, so a stop that waits for anything else stops the train from being ridden.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.rail.text_6: A train with a driver, two or more stations and a free seat becomes a way to travel. Residents ride it between its stations.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.rail.text_7: Riders get off at their station while the train waits. If a train is not ridden, Create's train map says why.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.rail.text_8: Trains under Facilities show each train's stations, whether it is running or stopped, and when it has no driver.
